ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast bimodal distribution; approximately 45% low-intensity (black/dark-gray) pixels concentrated on the left lobe and trailing edges versus 55% high-intensity (white/light-gray) pixels dominant on the right lobe.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: The left lobe is characterized by a contiguous dark-pigment mass with internal light mottling; the right lobe is predominantly high-intensity white with a distinct low-intensity dark band along the trailing edge and proximal to the median notch.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a calculated interior angle of approximately 65 degrees and significant vertical depth relative to the horizontal lobe span.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: The left lobe trailing edge displays high-amplitude, irregular serrations (jagged peaks); the right lobe trailing edge shows lower-amplitude, higher-frequency variations increasing toward the distal tip.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex outward curvature on both lobes; the left lobe exhibits a steeper vertical emergence angle from the water line, while the right lobe shows a more elongated horizontal sweep.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized clusters of circular high-intensity (white) pixels on the dark ventral surface of the left lobe, consistent with barnacle-related scarring.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Distinct dark linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) oriented vertically and diagonally across the light-pigmented regions of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: The left distal tip appears blunt and truncated; the right distal tip features an attached reddish-brown high-contrast organic cluster (likely cyamids or seaweed) extending beyond the natural fluke boundary.
other_distinctive_markers: The localized reddish-brown pixel mass on the trailing edge of the right fluke tip serves as a highly unique visual marker against the white ventral pigment.
